αἰὲν: αἰεί — always, ever; adv., epic by-form αἰέν (Attic ἀεί)
αἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj., epic/dialectal by-form αἰ (used before κε)
αὐτοὶ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., masc. nom. pl.: ’themselves’
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε
βίοτον: βίοτος — life, livelihood, substance one lives on; acc. sg.
βῆ: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔβη): ’went, strode’
γ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle (elided γ’)
γαίης: γαῖα — earth, land; gen. sg. (Ionic η for α)
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γενέσθαι: γίγνομαι — become, be born; aor. inf.: ’to have been born’
γλαυκῶπις: γλαυκῶπις — epithet of Athena: ’gleaming-eyed’ (or ’owl-eyed’; sense uncertain); fem. nom. sg.
γούνασι: γόνυ — knee; dat. pl., epic γούνασι (= Attic γόνασι)
δή: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δαΐφρονος: δαΐφρων — wise-minded, or perhaps ’warlike’; sense disputed (from δαῆναι ’learn’ or δάϊς ’battle’); masc. gen. sg.
διός: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; gen. sg. (stem Δι-)
δώμασιν: δῶμα — house, dwelling; neut. dat. pl. (plural for a single dwelling): ’over his house’
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῖα: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. nom. sg., epithet of goddesses and heroes
δῖος: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. nom. sg., epithet of heroes (= fem. δῖα)
δῶ: δῶ — house, home; indeclinable epic noun (= δῶμα), used as nom./acc. sg.
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also introducing an indirect question after a verb of asking or telling: ’whether’ (εἰ δή ’whether indeed’) · also in εἰ δ’ ἄγε, an interjectional idiom with the imperative: ’come now, well then’
εἰς: εἰς — into, to; prep. + acc. · also εἰμί ’be’: pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ): ’you are’ (τίς … εἰς; ’who are you?’)
εἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. (accented εἴ before a following enclitic, περ among them)
εἴπω: εἶπον — say, tell; aor. subj. 1 sg.
ηὔδα: αὐδάω — speak, say; impf. 3 sg., augmented (αὐ- → ηὐ-)
θυμὸς: θυμός — heart, spirit, desire; nom. sg.
θυμῷ: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; dat. sg.
κέ: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic
κέν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic
κακὸν: κακός — bad, evil; masc./neut. acc. sg.: ’by an evil (fate)’, inner acc. with μόρον
καλὸν: καλός — beautiful, fair, fine; masc. acc. sg. (agreeing with a noun) · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’beautifully’ (with an infinitive) · also neut. acc. sg. used as a noun, direct object: ’a fine one’ (μάλα καλὸν ἑλών)
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’)
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κεῖται: κεῖμαι — lie; pres. 3 sg., used of the dead: ’lies (dead)’ · also in the idiom θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται: ’rests with the gods, lies in the gods’ hands’ (of an outcome, not of the dead)
κλέος: κλέος — fame, renown, report; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. (same form), direct object: μέγα κλέος ἤρατο ’won great fame’; κλέος φέρειν ’bring report’
κράτος: κράτος — strength, power, might; neut. nom. sg.
κτεάτεσσιν: κτέαρ — possession, property; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι
κῆρ: κῆρ — heart; neut. acc. sg., accusative of respect (φίλον κῆρ ’in his own heart’)
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλιστα: μάλα — very, much; superl. adv. μάλιστα: ’most of all, especially’
μέγαρον: μέγαρον — hall, main room of the house; acc. sg.
μέντης: Μέντης — Mentes, a Taphian chieftain, the guise Athena takes; nom. sg.
μεγάροισιν: μέγαρον — hall, great room, house; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν), plural for a single house
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’
μύθων: μῦθος — speech, word, thing said (not yet ’myth’ in Homer); gen. pl.
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses
μᾶλλον: μάλα — very, much; comparative adv. μᾶλλον: ’more, rather, the more’
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg.
νήποινον: νήποινος — unpunished, without payment (νη- + ποινή); neut. acc. sg.
νεμεσήσεαι: νεμεσάω — feel indignation at, take amiss (+ dat.); fut. 2 sg. mid., uncontracted (= Attic νεμεσήσῃ)
νόστιμον: νόστιμος — of homecoming, of return; neut. acc. sg., in νόστιμον ἦμαρ ’day of return’
νύ: νυ — now, then; weak encl. particle
ξεῖνος: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); nom. sg.
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’)
οἶκον: οἶκος — house, household (and its stores); acc. sg.
οἶκόνδε: οἶκος — house, home; acc. sg. + suffix -δε ’towards’: ’homeward’
οἶος: οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. sg.
οἷον: οἷος — such as, of what sort; neut. as exclamatory adv.: ’how!, what a thing!’ (rough breathing; distinct from οἶος ’alone’)
οἷσιν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; possessive adj., neut./masc. dat. pl. (ν-movable): ’his own’ (agreeing with δώμασιν)
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὔτ: οὔτε (elided οὔτ’) — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
οὔτε: οὔτε — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
πάντες: πᾶς — all, every; masc. nom. pl.
πάϊς: παῖς — child, son; nom. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic παῖς)
παιδὸς: παῖς — child, daughter; fem. gen. sg. (φίλης ... παιδός ’a dear daughter’)
παλλὰς: Παλλάς — Pallas, title of Athena of unknown origin (perhaps πάλλω ’brandish’); nom. sg.
παρήμενος: πάρημαι — sit beside, sit near (+ dat.); pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
παρὰ: παρά — beside, along, from; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · also used as an adverb with no case expressed: ’beside, alongside’ (παρὰ … ἐτάνυσσε τράπεζαν ’drew a table up beside (them)’)
πεπνυμένος: πέπνυμαι — have one’s wits about one, be prudent; perf. part. masc. nom. sg. (trad. linked to πνέω ’breathe’, though uncertain), stock epithet: ’prudent’
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’)
πηνελόπεια: Πηνελόπεια — Penelope, wife of Odysseus; nom. sg.
ποθεν: πόθεν — from somewhere; indefinite enclitic adv. (accentless after εἰ), distinct from interrogative πόθεν ’from where?’
πολλοὶ: πολύς — much, many; masc. nom. pl.
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’
ποτε: ποτέ — once, at some time, formerly; enclitic adv.
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
προσηύδα: προσαυδάω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg.
πόσιν: πόσις — husband; acc. sg. · also the distinct noun πόσις ’a drinking, drink’ (from πίνω); acc. sg.: ’drink’ (paired with βρῶσις ’eating’)
πᾶσι: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl.
σ: σύ — you (sg.); encl. acc. sg., elided (σ’ = σε): ’you’
σέ: σύ — you (sg.); acc. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’you’ (σέ γε τοῖον ἐγείνατο ’bore a son such as you’)
σοὶ: σύ — you (sg.); dat. sg.: ’to, for you’
στῆ: ἵστημι — set, stand; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔστη): ’stood’
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’
τά: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.; also relative: ’which’ (accented τά before a following enclitic)
τέ: τε — and; enclitic connective, also marks a standing fact (epic τε)
τί: τίς, τί — who? what?; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially ’why’ · also the enclitic indefinite τις, τι ’someone, something’ (accented τί before an enclitic): neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a negative, ’at all’ (οὔ τι)
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
ταφίοισι: Τάφιοι — the Taphians, an island people led by Mentes; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι
ταῦτα: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τηλέμαχος: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; nom. sg.
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg.
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοῖσι: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’to/among them’
τοῦ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. gen. sg. ’of him, that one’
τοῦτ: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. acc. sg., elided (τοῦτ’ = τοῦτο)
τοῦτο: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. sg.
τροίης: Τροία — Troy; gen. sg. (Ionic -ης for Attic -ας)
τόδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. sg.
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these things, of them’
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’)
φίλον: φίλος — dear, one’s own (with kin/body parts serves as a possessive); neut. nom./acc. sg.
φιλέεσκε: φιλέω — love, be fond of; impf. 3 sg., iterative in -σκ- (unaugmented): ’used to be fond of’
φιληρέτμοισιν: φιλήρετμος — oar-loving, fond of the oar (φίλος + ἐρετμόν); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν
φρεσὶ: φρήν — mind, heart, wits; fem. dat. pl.
φρεσὶν: φρήν — mind, heart, wits (lit. midriff); fem. dat. pl.
χερσίν: χείρ — hand; fem. dat. pl., ν-movable
χόλον: χόλος — anger, wrath (lit. gall, bile); acc. sg.
ἀέκοντα: ἄκων — unwilling; masc. acc. sg., epic ἀέκων (= Attic ἄκοντα): ’against his will’
ἀγχιάλοιο: Ἀγχίαλος — Anchialus, father of Mentes, ’near the sea’; gen. sg., epic -οιο
ἀθήνη: Ἀθήνη — Athena, goddess of wisdom and war; nom. sg.
ἀμφίπολος: ἀμφίπολος — handmaid, woman in attendance; nom. sg.
ἀνθρώποισι: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἀντίον: ἀντίον — face to face, in answer, opposite; adv.
ἀνὰ: ἀνά — up along, throughout; prep. + acc.
ἀτὰρ: ἀτάρ — but, and; epic conj. (by-form of αὐτάρ)
ἀχαιῶν: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἄλλα: ἄλλος — other, another; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἄλλοι: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. pl.
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἅμα: ἅμα — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐγὼν: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg., form used before a vowel
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat.
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’)
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐστίν: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg., ν-movable form
ἐόντας: εἰμί — be; pres. part. acc. pl. masc., epic (= Attic ὄντας)
ἑ: ἕ — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. sg. reflexive/personal pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/-ήν/-ό)
ἑὸν: ἑός — his own, her own (possessive, by-form of ὅς); masc. acc. sg.
ἔβαν: βαίνω — go, walk; aor. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἔβησαν)
ἔγνω: γιγνώσκω — come to know, learn, perceive; aor. 3 sg., no augment
ἔδοντες: ἔδω — eat (epic, = Attic ἐσθίω); pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’eating’
ἔμμεναι: εἰμί — be; pres. inf., epic (= Attic εἶναι)
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔπειτ: ἔπειτα (elided ἔπειτ’) — then, next, after that
ἔτ: ἔτι — still, yet; adv., elided (ἔτ’ = ἔτι)
ἔφαθ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἔφατο, elided ἔφαθ’, τ>θ before rough breathing)
ἔχῃσιν: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. subj. 3 sg., epic ending -ῃσι (= Attic ἔχῃ)
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg.
ἥν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (fem. acc. sg.)
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’
ἦμαρ: ἦμαρ — day (epic for ἡμέρα); neut. nom./acc. sg.
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσῆα: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; acc. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆα)
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg.
ὃν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (masc. acc. sg.)
ὄλοντο: ὄλλυμι — destroy; mid. perish, be destroyed; aor. 3 pl. mid., no augment
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj.
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη)
ὅδ: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., masc. nom. sg., elided (ὅδ’ = ὅδε)
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅπως: ὅπως — so that, in order that, how; + subj. or fut. indic.
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.)
ὅττι: ὅστις — whoever, whatever; epic neut. nom./acc. sg. ὅττι (= Attic ὅ τι)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥα: ἄρα — then, so; weak enclitic form ῥα (used after a vowel)
